target.archival_interpretation: cylindrical support/component of a multipart assemblage with a through-socket and ring seats; likely originally joined to additional upper/lower elements

acquisition_batch.transaction: Acquired from M. & F. Dosseur, 5 rue de Lille; objects previously ceded by Maurice Nahman of Cairo
acquisition_batch.finding: The contiguous inventory range is a heterogeneous dealer-acquisition batch, not one archaeological or physical assemblage. Inventory adjacency therefore cannot be used as evidence of physical compatibility.

inventory_screen.special_provenance_note: IFAO Karnak Cachette records a 1904 Legrain-find attribution; demonstrates object-specific provenance inside the dealer batch

inventory_screen.reason: Near width coincidence (11.6 vs E11072 11.7 cm) is outweighed by incompatible material, period, morphology and Memphis manufacture.

reconstruction_result.meaning: No catalogued object in the same contiguous acquisition range is a credible surviving upper caisse/bassin or lower base for E 11072.
not_proven: that no mate survives elsewhere in Louvre collections
that the missing elements were acquired in 1905
that E 11072 was excavated at Abydos
that 'reliquaire d'Abydos' is a secure findspot rather than typological/functional naming

archival_route.fonds: Archives des musees nationaux, Departement des Antiquites egyptiennes du musee du Louvre (serie AE)
archival_route.important_correction: 20144775/8 is demonstrably a broad archival container including substantially earlier nineteenth-century acquisition correspondence (e.g. Mariette/Hauterive material). Therefore the range 8-10 must not be cited as if it already proves that Nahman/Dosseur correspondence is present; document-level identification is still required.

next_gate.name: E11072_LOST_MATE_OR_ARCHIVAL_ASSEMBLAGE_IDENTITY_GATE
required: Locate document-level 1905 acquisition correspondence/register attachments for Nahman -> Dosseur -> Louvre.
Extract any drawings, dimensions, seller descriptions, grouping marks, provenance statements or mention of detached/missing parts for E 11072.
Search Louvre collection outside E 11057-E 11073 for diorite/stone Osirian reliquary components with compatible circular seats/socket geometry and pre-1905 or 1905 provenance.
Treat geometric compatibility as necessary but not sufficient; require material, chronology, join morphology and provenance consistency.
If no surviving mate appears, reconstruct only as a bounded hypothetical multipart geometry and label missing parts UNKNOWN.
